data.author: davidlange6

ONNX Runtime's CPU arena grows in power-of-two chunks to fit the largest activations seen and by default keeps that memory for the whole job. data.title: PythiaInterface: print statistics once at finalize, not per event
data.author: kjvbrt
data.body:
Hi,

BEGINRELEASENOTES
 - `PythiaInterface`: print the Pythia statistics once in `finalize()` instead of after every event.
 - `PythiaInterface`: deprecate the `printPythiaStatistics` property; it has no effect and only prints a warning when set.
 - `PythiaInterface`: add `printPythiaStatisticsEveryNEvents` (default 0 = disabled) to also print the statistics every N events.

ENDRELEASENOTES

`printPythiaStatistics` called `Pythia::stat()` from `getNextEvent()`, so it printed the full statistics block after every generated event. At scale (e.g. 100k events/job) this floods stdout and can overrun a job's captured-output buffer, killing the job partway through.

data.title: ACTSDuplicateRemoval: never keep two equal tracks
data.author: jbeirer
data.body:
BEGINRELEASENOTES

- `ACTSDuplicateRemoval` no longer keeps two equal tracks (more than half of the hits of the shorter one shared). A track is now dropped if an equal kept track is at least as good, and otherwise replaces all equal kept tracks.

ENDRELEASENOTES

Two ways the old loop kept duplicates:

- a better track replaced the *first* equal kept track and stopped, so further kept tracks equal to it stayed;
- a worse track did not stop at the first equal one and could replace a later one, so the kept list then held two tracks equal to each other.

This happens when partial tracks of one particle are around (they are not equal to each other, but both are equal to the full track): two full copies can each replace one of them and both survive.
